claims.claim_text: The measured fraction of the ES2020 observable surface the engine executes is published as a single content-addressed, gated coverage figure, broken into six weighted category views (parser, builtin, control-flow, async, module, intentional-divergence) with a floor that exposes the weakest view.

claims.reason: A reproducible, content-addressed weighted coverage summary is linked (docs/coverage/es2020_coverage_summary_bundle_v1, bd-fqlfw.7.4). On the ES2020-normative tc39/test262 profile (language/* + built-ins/*) the engine EXECUTES 6201/47514 = 130508 millionths (~13.0508%) of the observable surface, where executed = evaluated without an engine error (positive) or correctly rejected (negative); assertion outcomes are not verified, so this is an execution-coverage measure, NOT a conformance pass-rate (the stricter harness-based ES2020 conformance pass-rate is far lower, ~0.25%, docs/test262_real_corpus_pass_rate_v1.json). Weakest view 'builtin' at 16664 millionths. Six weighted views plus the floor prevent a single gamed percentage; stays target. Gated by ./scripts/run_coverage_summary_bundle_gate.sh ci.

freshness_eprocess_policy.note: Per-claim freshness is COMPUTED from each committed bundle's real timestamp (manifest generated_at_utc, falling back to the artifact's git commit time) and judged by an anytime-valid e-process boundary, never authored. Each elapsed day contributes a log-LR increment ln(1/alpha)/horizon toward staleness; freshness is rejected once the e-value reaches 1/alpha (false-staleness-alarm probability <= alpha). See crates/franken-engine/src/claim_evidence_lattice.rs::FreshnessEProcess (bd-sde5e.1.4).
